title: Computational Data Analysis Core
text: Computational Data Analysis Core (CDAC) (Core #4) The Computational Data Analysis Core (CDAC) at the University of North Dakota (UND) was established in 2022 during the Host-Pathogen Interactions (HPI) COBRE Phase 2 to support bioinformatics and big data analysis for project leaders and the larger COBRE community. Since its induction in 2022, the Core has supported 25 projects for 15 principal investigator users, contributing to 12 peer-reviewed publications. In parallel, we have developed 11 customized analysis pipelines. Our proven track record during Phase 2 positions us to further enhance our capabilities, sustainability, and outreach in COBRE Phase 3. Our goals for Phase 3 are to (1) enhance and expand advanced bioinformatics services and training, (2) establish revenue for bioinformatics, and (3) broaden the core’s user base and strengthen collaborative networks. CDAC has already benefited research at UND and established itself as a trusted resource by providing state-of-the-art computational analyses of omics data, fostering collaborations between UND and external institutions, and educating investigators through training, workshops, and seminars. In Phase 3, we will measure success using key metrics, including number of analyses performed, unique investigators served, revenue generated, training event participation, and new collaborations, and use these metrics to demonstrate reduced reliance on external funding, attainment of fiscal sustainability, and continued support of advanced data-analysis needs across the regional research community, further advancing host-pathogen interactions and systems biology research at UND.

title: Strategies to Reduce Global Health Disparities in Cervical Cancer
text:
The presence of HPV16 variants was correlated both with reductions in the INFγ ELISPOT
responses and lower rates of viral clearance in individuals vaccinated with the therapeutic vaccine
based on the European strain. Here, we will characterize the impact of natural variants in HPV16
E6/E7 oncogenic proteins on the immune evasion and the carcinogenesis in mice transgenic for
different human MHC-1 molecules. Our goal is to develop a therapeutic vaccine highly effective in
geographically, ethnically, and racially diverse populations at clearing HPV16, regardless of E6/E7
variant, to comprehensively intercept HPV16 associated carcinogenesis.

title: Extending Real-Time fMRI Neurofeedback Training into Real-World Contexts
text:
Real-time fMRI neurofeedback (rtfMRI-nf) is a powerful tool for training individuals to modulate targeted brain
activity—such as reward responding in the nucleus accumbens (NAcc)—but sustaining these effects beyond
the scanner and into daily life remains a key challenge. This study tests a phone-based ecological momentary
intervention designed to extend rtfMRI-nf training into real-world contexts among young adults who use
alcohol. Results will provide critical insights into scalable, neuroscience-informed strategies to strengthen
reward-related self-regulation and reduce alcohol misuse and related risk behaviors.

title: Targeted RNA delivery using ribonucleoprotein
text:
This project aims to address the major problem of biologics delivery for cancer treatment and management by
developing a new class of biomimetic nanocarrier, RNP. Compared to prior arts, this delivery technology
avoids the cationic charges yet still achieving all the desired functionalities for combinatorial siRNA therapy.

title: Defining the roles of host factors and innate immune signaling in the ocular tropism of enterovirus D70
text:
Enterovirus D70 (EVD70) is a highly contagious human enterovirus that causes acute hemorrhagic
conjunctivitis, a painful and debilitating ocular disease. This proposal aims to elucidate mechanisms by which
EVD70 infects ocular cells, define the role of a novel host factor, JTB, in mediating EVD70 infection, and
explore host-virus interactions in corneal organoids that model the human ocular surface. These studies will
improve our understanding of EVD70 infection and identify pathways that can be targeted to develop novel
antiviral therapeutics.

title: Defining determinants of the lineage identity program in lung cancer and therapeutic resistance
text:
Mutation in LKB1/STK11 is one of the most frequent causal genetic alterations in Non-Small Cell
Lung Cancer, and is associated with therapeutic resistance to stand-of-care therapies and poor
patient outcome. The proposed study will elucidate the molecular mechanism(s) through which
LKB1 mutation and therapeutic resistance regulate HDAC3/NKX2-1 function to control lung tumor
growth. This work aims to generate mechanistic and biological understanding as a foundation
from which to develop improved therapeutic options for patients with LKB1/STK11 mutant lung
cancer.

title: Regulation of Dental Pulp Stem Cell Polarization for Tubular Dentin Regeneration
text:
This proposal aims to understand and control dental pulp stem cell (DPSC) polarization and differentiation, and
regenerate functional tubular dentin using DPSCs. Completion of this project will significantly facilitate the
development of innovative biomaterials for regenerative endodontics, therefore, improve the health of hundreds
of millions of people in US.

title: Using real-time data capture to examine affective mechanisms as mediators of physical activity maintenance in interventions
text:
Long-term maintenance of regular physical activity significantly lowers risks of cancer and chronic diseases.
Public heath guidelines recommend at least 150 min/week of moderate-to-vigorous intensity physical activity,
without addressing the affective experiences (i.e., how people feel) during the behavior, which may be crucial
for maintaining behavior change. This early-phase trial will determine the content and dose of affect-based digital
intervention treatments needed to target affective mechanisms and sustain physical activity maintenance among
adults at elevated cancer risk due to inactivity and overweight/obesity.

title: Monitoring of Glaucoma Patients in Advanced Disease
text:
The proposed project will develop algorithms for predicting and detecting glaucomatous progression in
advanced glaucoma eyes tested longitudinally with visual field and optical imaging technologies and will make
use of a very large amount of data, to do so. This proposal addresses the current NEI Glaucoma and Optic
Neuropathies Program objectives of developing improved diagnostic measures to characterize and detect optic
nerve disease onset and characterize glaucomatous neuro- degeneration within the visual pathways at
structural and functional levels. Characterization of functional, structural, and microvascular loss in the central
area of the retina and development of a clinically useful, novel, empirical system for predicting and detecting
glaucomatous progression in advanced glaucoma will have a significant impact on the future of clinical care
and reduce the burden of the disease.

title: Identifying Risk and Resilience Markers of Suicidal Ideation and Behavior in Veterans:  A  Longitudinal Study of Natural Language Processing and Neurophysiology
text:
In 2021, nearly 18 Veterans died by suicide every day, underscoring the urgent need to improve suicide
prevention. Suicide attempts (SA) occur in only 12% of individuals with suicidal ideation (SI) and pose a
particularly high risk for suicide, as SA may reflect a “capability for suicide”. SA may be related to abnormal
emotion arousal and regulation which can be studied using psychophysiological measures, such as EEG and
startle, and also, linguistic measures. We propose the first longitudinal study to examine language use and
psychophysiology together to assess emotional arousal and regulation in a cohort of Veterans with mood and
anxiety disorders who are at a range of risk for suicide: 1) low (no SI or SA); 2) moderate (SI only); 3) high (SA
in the past 5 years + SI). Our multi-modal design promises to identify linguistic and underlying neurophysiological
features which index emotion arousal and regulation and are indicative of SI and behavior in Veterans. The
proposed research has the potential to significantly improve future suicide prevention intervention strategies.

title: Basal Ganglia - Brainstem Networks in the Control of Seizures
text:
Project Narrative. Epilepsy is the second most common neurological disorder, but unfortunately, current
treatments for epilepsy cannot control seizures in many patients. For this reason, identifying new methods and
targets to control seizures is a high priority. Here we will activate a brain circuit that controls brain arousal and
determine if doing so prevents seizures in several animal models, while simultaneously determining the
connections in the brain that enable this circuit to stop seizures.

title: Improving social connectedness through digital health to enhance recovery from OUD among the justice involved population.
text:
People with a history of Opioid Use Disorder and criminal justice involvement are more likely to experience
loneliness following release from jail/prison leading to negative outcomes such as treatment dropout and
increased substance use. Providing peer recovery support, particularly through a highly accessible, digital
health platform, is a potential way to decrease loneliness in this population. The current study seeks to test
whether a mobile peer recovery support app, delivered to individuals with a recent history of taking medication
for opioid use disorder while in jail/prison, will improve outcomes for this vulnerable population.

title: Multiome measurements connecting transcription start sites at single-nucleotide resolution, DNA methylation and open chromatin status to splicing outcome across single cells in health and disease
text:
DNA methylation, chromatin, transcription initiation and alternative splicing form a tightly linked triangle and
single-cell genomics has revolutionized modern-day biology. However, to-date we are lacking a precise
understanding of the relationships between the above modalities in the cell types that form complex tissue. Here,
we devise new single-cell technology to measure multiple modalities to infer the relationships between them in
health and disease.

title: Elucidating the contributions of genetic variation to congenital heart disease causality and outcomes
text:
Genetic variation plays important roles in causing congenital heart disease, the commonest class of birth
defects, as well as in cardiac and non-cardiac outcomes among affected individuals. For this program project,
a highly collaborative group of investigators will use existing genetic data, clinical data derived from electronic
medical records and for neuroimaging and discarded cardiac tissues from infants who underwent open-heart
surgery to advance our understanding of which genetic factors drive congenital heart disease’s origins and
outcomes. These advances will lead to better care for affected individuals and their families, ending
diagnostic odysseys and providing opportunities for novel therapeutic approaches.

title: Function and regulatory mechanisms of the Wnt5a-Ror morphogenetic pathway
text:
Function and regulatory mechanisms of the Wnt5a-Ror morphogenetic pathway
PI: Ho
Wnt5a-Ror signaling is an evolutionarily conserved developmental signaling pathway that controls cell and tissue
morphogenesis. Genetic mutations that disrupt the pathway cause congenital birth defects. Our research aims
to delineate the cell biological functions and regulatory mechanisms of the pathway and how these fundamental
processes are perturbed in Wnt5a-Ror driven human diseases.

title: Painful Versus Insensate Diabetic Neuropathy
text:
Peripheral axon loss, poor sensation and pain are all components associated with diabetic peripheral
neuropathy and new treatment approaches to correct these complications are desperately needed. We will
determine if ketones bodies have direct actions on sensory neurons to improve their metabolism, stimulate axon
growth, improve sensation and reduce pain.

title: Dissect the mechanisms underlying interspecies pluripotent stem cell competition
text:
Cell competition, the process of eliminating viable but “less fit” neighbor cells, has been proposed as a
surveillance mechanism to ensure normal development and also has been suggested to act as a barrier to
interspecies chimerism. We uncovered a previously unknown mode of cell competition between pluripotent stem
cells from different species. This project aims to decipher the underlying molecular mechanisms and develop
effective strategy to enable interspecies organogenesis by suppressing interspecies cell competition.

title: Neural and computational mechanisms underlying robust object recognition
text:
This project will provide a detailed characterization of human behavioral and neural responses to real-world
object images degraded by visual noise or blur, with the goal of developing deep neural network (DNN)
recognition models that can better approximate the robust neural computations performed by the human visual
system. The foundational knowledge gained from this research will inform our understanding of central visual
disorders, including both acquired and neurodevelopmental disorders. The development of more robust,
human-like DNN models is also of considerable relevance to AI applications in computer vision, including the
analysis and evaluation of medical images.

title: Project 4 - Mechanisms of establishing clonal dominance
text: Hematopoietic clonal imbalance predisposes individuals to hematopoietic disorders, some progressing to myelodysplasia. During aging, mutations arise that lead to clonal dominance. In transplantation or gene therapy trials, clonal alterations complicate therapy. Somatic genetic mutation(s) may bestow a selective growth advantage to a single hematopoietic stem cell so that it will eventually outgrow normal (wild type, WT) cells causing clonal imbalance. Early detection of such cells is key to therapeutically intervene to block progression to a blood disorder. The Zebrabow zebrafish allows color barcoding and tracking of individual hematopoietic stem cells during differentiation into peripheral blood cells in vivo. A recently developed technique called TWISTR allows mosaic targeting of genes in the Zebrabow genetic background. Without the need for transplantation, a robust competition assay between WT and single gene mutant hematopoietic stem cells can be monitored using the color-based cellular barcoding TWISTR system. The dominant clone can be sorted via flow cytometry and compared to non-dominant clones for downstream analysis. Mosaic mutagenesis of ASXL1 leads to clonal dominance, and we found that inhibition of the NR4A1 anti-inflammatory pathway using CRISPR or chemical inhibition restores clonal balance. Using metabolomics, we have found that choline metabolism is altered in dominant asxl1 mutant clones. In Aim 1, pharmacologic experiments will be performed to evaluate the NR4A1 pathway in facilitating clonal dominance and genetic experiments targeting choline-related metabolic genes will identify metabolic targets for suppressing clonal dominance. We also found that macrophages play a role in stem cell clonality through physical interactions with hematopoietic stem cells. Macrophages interact with the “eat me” signal, Calreticulin, on the surface of hematopoietic stem cells to determine their fate. In Aim 2, we plan to evaluate mutants of Calreticulin orthologs and examine the effects on clonality. We plan to probe the mechanism of the induced clone expansion after macrophage interactions. We also have undertaken a chemical genetic screen to find inducers of Calreticulin on the surface of zebrafish and human hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells and will study specific compounds that can induce an “eat-me” signal for dominant clones. Our studies will have an impact on the basic understanding of clonal balance and will lead to potential therapies for clonal dominance.

title: Injectable scaffolds for early detection of immune dysregulation and monitoring response to immunotherapies
text:
Type 1 diabetes mellitus (T1D) is an autoimmune disease in which patients, usually children but often adults,
present acutely ill due to symptoms of hyperglycemia or diabetic ketoacidosis, which occurs because of
destruction of the insulin-producing -cells of the pancreatic islets. The diagnosis of T1D occurs too late for
prevention, which necessitates managing the disease with lifelong use of insulin and addressing the severe
macrovascular and microvascular complications. We propose to develop a technology to monitor for disease
initiation prior to -cell destruction, allowing the application of therapies that can prevent or delay disease
progression.
